reports.name: USDA Weekly Export Sales (Thanksgiving week — date may shift)

outlook: Wheat is bouncing at midday Thursday after Wednesday's dollar-driven selloff pushed Chicago and Kansas City wheat to eight-month lows: Minneapolis December spring wheat is up about 12 cents near $6.41 and Chicago December up 8 cents near $5.78, helped by weekly wheat export sales of 345,000 tonnes (up 89%) and a Ukrainian ministry warning that its 2027 wheat crop could fall about a third to 17 million tonnes. December corn is up about 3.5 cents near $4.39 after hitting a 4.5-month low Wednesday, with weekly export sales of 1.59 million tonnes in line with expectations. January soybeans are off 3 cents near $12.14 despite strong weekly sales of 1.5 million tonnes, as Brazil rains support a record crop outlook and traders wait for any farm-purchase news from Thursday's Trump–Xi meeting at APEC. ICE January canola is up about C$7 near C$778 per tonne, while the U.S. dollar index sits near a 19-month high.
